disclaimer: Design bounds cited from public sources for a decision-support demo. NOT a compliance tool: it does not certify Title 24, ASHRAE 90.1, NFPA 101, CBC or CFC compliance. A lighting designer sets final setback floors after a photometric check; the AHJ resolves code conflicts.

life_safety.meaning: means of egress illuminated at >= 1 fc (11 lux) at the walking surface whenever the building space it serves is occupied
stairways need >= 10 fc during conditions of stair use (new stairs)
motion switches allowed in egress only if fail-safe (lights on when the sensor fails), timer >= 15 min, and activated by any occupant movement
a motion-sensor fault, stale data or controller loss sends the zone to full output and raises an alarm (fail-safe)
life_safety.cite: NFPA 101 7.8.1.2.2 fail-safe; pattern mirrors T24 120.6(c) CO-sensor failure reset

life_safety.meaning: emergency lighting lasts >= 90 min, initial average 1 fc, minimum 0.1 fc (some existing buildings: 60 min, CFC 1104.5.1)
UL 924 bypass/shunt relays force emergency lights on at loss of normal power whatever the controls do; Cerebro never writes to emergency, exit-sign or egress-floor circuits
up to 0.1 W/ft2 may stay on continuously in areas designated as means of egress; egress lighting must still meet CBC 1008 in partial-off mode

basis.cite: Title 24 130.1(c)6C: corridors and stairwells reduce lighting power by >= 50% when vacant; sensors cover every egress path
NFPA 101 7.8.1.2.2: >= 15 min fail-safe timer in egress
vacant level 0.5 = the shallowest compliant setback; deeper only after a photometric check keeps >= 1 fc
Title 24 130.1(c)6C: stairwells reduce by >= 50% when vacant
CFC 1008.2.1 / NFPA 101 7.8.1.3: >= 10 fc during stair use; >= 1 fc egress floor at all other occupied times
treated like a corridor: the lobby is part of the exit path (exit discharge) so the 1 fc floor and 15 min fail-safe hold apply
Title 24 130.1(c)7B: a control step between 20% and 50% of design lighting power, zones of <= 500 W; 130.1(c)7 sets no off-delay

ASHRAE 90.1-2019 9.4.1.2: >= 50% reduction after 10 min without activity, zones <= 3,600 ft2 (conflicts with the NFPA 15 min egress timer where 90.1 governs; the AHJ resolves it). In LA, Title 24 governs, so the 15 min fail-safe hold is kept
vacant level 0.3 chosen inside the 0.2-0.5 step
Title 24 130.1(c)5: restrooms turn fully off within 20 min of vacancy (not egress-designated here)
hold 15 min: inside the 20 min maximum
Title 24 130.1(c)5 full-off rule (classrooms, conference and multipurpose rooms, small offices, restrooms) applied to amenity rooms

demand_response.cite: 2025 Title 24: demand-responsive lighting >= 15% reduction for >= 4,000 W general lighting; DR controls certified to OpenADR 2.0b (110.12(a)1B). Egress zones are never trimmed (team rule).

hvac_standby.ventilation_condition: ventilation may stay off only while the space temperature is between the active heating and cooling setpoints
hvac_standby.applicability: spaces with occupant-sensor ventilation control under 120.1(d)5; not a blanket rule for corridors or lobbies

garage_ventilation.failure_action: return to design ventilation and raise an alarm (15 ppm divergence rules)
